title: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas
hookLine: sick and ready to give all his wealth away, he was told: a third is plenty (Bukhari)

lines: A THIRD, AND A THIRD IS A LOT.
cards: A man lies sick in Mecca, so sick he fears he will die there. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, comes to visit. And the sick man, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, has a plan ready.
I have a lot of wealth, he says, and only one daughter to inherit from me. Shall I give two thirds of it away in charity? No.
A third, the Prophet says, and a third is a lot. Today: a generous man stopped, kindly, from being too generous.

teach.b: Sa'd tells this himself, in Sahih al-Bukhari. He is ill and wants to do the most good he can with what he has left. The Prophet doesn't say: wonderful, give it all.
He bargains him down, and then gives the reason, the heart of the day.

teach.h: BETTER TO LEAVE YOUR HEIRS WELL OFF.
teach.b: It is better to leave your heirs well off than to leave them poor, holding out their hands to people. The daughter matters. Charity that leaves your own people begging has missed something.

teach.h: EVEN THE BITE TO YOUR WIFE'S MOUTH.
teach.b: Then a second line, just as surprising: whatever you spend seeking God's pleasure, you are rewarded for it, even the bite of food you lift to your wife's mouth. So feeding your family is not the opposite of charity.
It counts. Sa'd also feared dying in Mecca, the city he had left when he emigrated. The Prophet told him he might live on, so that some people would benefit through him and others be harmed.
Tradition says he did live on.

teach.h: WHY A BEQUEST STOPS AT A THIRD.
teach.b: Muslim jurists use this visit as a foundation for the rule that a person may leave no more than a third of their estate as a bequest, with the rest passing to heirs by the shares the Qur'an sets.
Different schools work out the details differently, but the third is traced back to this room. Generous enough to matter. Careful enough to leave no one behind.

how: In Islamic law a person may leave up to a third of their estate as a bequest, for charity or for people outside the fixed shares; the rest passes to heirs by the shares set in the Qur'an. Schools differ on the details.

games.q: what does “sa'd ibn abi waqqas” mean?
o: the heir who received a third of a large estate
the companion who gave all his wealth on his deathbed
the companion told that a third of his wealth is a lot

games.q: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas — tap the pairs.
p: and a third is a lot
better left well off than begging
a bite to his wife's mouth

s: the Prophet told Sa'd to give everything away
he bargained him down to a third, and said a third is a lot.
feeding your own family can count as rewarded spending
even the bite you lift to your wife's mouth, the Prophet told Sa'd.
Sa'd died of that illness in Mecca
he was told he might live on so that some would benefit through him, and tradition says he did live on.

games.q: you're Sa'd, very sick and afraid of dying in Mecca, with one daughter to inherit. you ask whether to give two thirds of your wealth away. what do you expect to hear?
o: a third, and a third is a lot.
give nothing; keep it all for her.
games.why: the Prophet said no to two thirds and no to half: a third, and a third is a lot. better to leave your heirs well off.

practice: Think of the places where you give: money, time, energy, attention. Look honestly for one where you give so much that the people closest to you go without, or one where you give nothing at all, and picture one small adjustment.
If you pray, you can ask for wisdom in giving.

wordCard.voice: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. The companion who, sick in Mecca, wanted to give away most of his wealth, and was told a third is a lot, and that feeding his family counts too. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the third, the word at the center of Sa'd's conversation.

carryVoice: Your line: a third is plenty. Feeding your own family counts too. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2742 / 1295 / 5354 (Sa'd's illness; two thirds, half, a third; 'a third is a lot'; heirs well off; the bite to your wife's mouth)
